metadata.dataset: NASA LRO / LOLA & Mars MOLA Topography and Artemis Candidate Zones
metadata.source: NASA Artemis Candidate Landing Regions & Mars 2020 Perseverance Science Team

sites.name: Shackleton Crater Rim
sites.illuminationCitation: Mazarico et al. (2011), Icarus 211(2), Table 2 and Figure 6 (~86-92% at 2m mast height on rim point 1)
sites.missionRelevance: Prime Artemis landing zone. Features Peaks of Eternal Light with continuous solar power adjacent to permanently shadowed cryogenic ice reserves in the crater floor (40 Kelvin).

sites.name: Malapert Mountain (Peak of Malapert)
sites.illuminationCitation: Bussey et al. (1999), Geophysical Research Letters 26(9), Figure 3 and Mazarico et al. (2011) Table 2 (peak estimated ~85-89%)
sites.missionRelevance: Continuous direct line-of-sight to Earth for uninterruptible high-bandwidth communications, and ideal radio-quiet far side proximity.

sites.name: Nobile Crater Rim 1
sites.illuminationCitation: Gläser et al. (2018), Planetary and Space Science 162, Figure 7 and Colaprete et al. (2021) Table 1 (illumination ~75-80%)
sites.missionRelevance: NASA VIPER rover primary exploration target for subsurface neutron spectrometer volatile mapping.

sites.name: Haworth Crater Interior
sites.illuminationCitation: Colaprete et al. (2010), Science 330(6003), Fig 1 & Diviner PSR maps (permanently shadowed, ~0% direct sunlight)
sites.hazardRating: High (Total darkness, extreme cryogenic 35K temperature, boulder fields)
sites.missionRelevance: Highest water ice concentration in the south polar region. Requires nuclear power or beamed laser power to operate.
sites.instrument: LCROSS Impact plume spectrometry & Diviner radiometer

sites.name: Connecting Ridge (Shackleton-de Gerlache)
sites.illuminationCitation: Mazarico et al. (2011), Figure 7 (Shackleton-de Gerlache connecting ridge average ~82-86%)
sites.missionRelevance: Natural transit corridor connecting Shackleton rim and de Gerlache crater for rover logistics.

sites.name: Mare Tranquillitatis (Apollo 11 Base)
sites.illuminationCitation: Apollo 11 ALSEP Preliminary Science Report (NASA SP-214) & Heiken et al. (1991) Lunar Sourcebook Section 3.1 (~50% diurnal duty cycle, ~354h daylight / ~354h night)
sites.hazardRating: High (354-hour continuous lunar night, -180°C deep freeze)
sites.missionRelevance: Historical Apollo 11 landing site. Represents typical lunar equatorial maria, subjected to brutal 14-day days and 14-day nights requiring massive battery or nuclear systems.
sites.instrument: Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) & LRO LROC

sites.name: Jezero Crater Delta
sites.illuminationCitation: Farley et al. (2020), Space Science Reviews 216(8), Figure 4 (~43% annual average accounting for 25.19° obliquity and dust optical depth)
sites.hazardRating: Moderate (Delta escarpment, sand dunes, thermal inertia variations)
sites.missionRelevance: Mars 2020 Perseverance landing site. Ancient lacustrine clay-rich fan delta optimal for sample return and MOXIE atmospheric oxygen extraction.

sites.name: Arcadia Planitia
sites.illuminationCitation: Bramson et al. (2015), Geophysical Research Letters 42(16), Table 1 (~41% annual average at 39°N with seasonal solar declination)
sites.missionRelevance: Vast sheets of pure water ice buried just 1-2.5 meters beneath dust cover, easily accessible for SpaceX Starship and human ISRU base.
sites.instrument: Mars Odyssey GRS & MRO SHARAD Radar
